catalog_coverage.why: Prompt 1 names the existing personal rules file and explicitly requires overwrite in place; prompt 2 writes no file.
Claude is assigned the session and site reads; the student is not assigned manual proofreading for correctness.
Prompt 1 explicitly says to find what is wrong and not defend the rules file; prompt 2 asks for a generic line and the surrounding prose tells the student to trust their own gut.
Prompt 1's review questions are an internal audit checklist for Claude, not a sequential interview of the student.
Prompt 1 gives the destination and says to overwrite it in place; prompt 2 has no file-write destination.
Prompt 1 is a multi-move retro with an opening no-preamble cue but no final-line suppressor or nearby preamble primer; prompt 2 is short and bounded.
Prompt 1 explicitly says to overwrite in place, rewrite the file, and not append a retro-notes section.
Neither prompt invokes plan mode; prompt 1 explicitly disallows a plan.
Neither prompt requests sourced factual claims or citations.
The evidence-backed Debrief carve-out applies: prompt 1 requires comparison with the actual session and artifact-level dropped, sharpened, and added changes; prompt 2 requests quoted site lines.
Neither prompt offers a default structure or candidate answer for Claude to accept uncritically.
Neither prompt produces a plan for approval.
The prompts read the student's own session artifact and site; they do not ingest heterogeneous external sources.
Prompt 1 explicitly assumes the rules file is at least 30% wrong or thin and says not to defend it; prompt 2 uses an independent cold subagent and contrasting quoted lines.
